Q03.question: Describe battle from ambush through removal: foiling, early ending, dice limits, extra hits, removal priorities and who scores removed buildings/tokens.

rulings.ruling: To initiate, choose a clearing containing your warriors or pawn and an enemy as defender; you need not rule it. The defender may play one ambush matching the clearing (birds are wild). The attacker may foil with a matching ambush. The defender’s ambush is discarded either way; if foiled it deals no hits. Otherwise it immediately deals two hits, uncapped by defending warriors, and is discarded. If no attacking warriors or pawns remain after ambush, battle ends immediately.
rulings.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle

rulings.ruling: Resolve applicable before-roll effects (attacker chooses their order if both players have them), roll (higher die is attacker’s hits, lower is defender’s, ties give equal hits), then resolve after-roll effects with attacker choosing order if both players have them. Each side’s rolled hits are capped by its own warriors in battle; Alliance defending reverses dice, while Vagabond uses undamaged swords instead of warriors. Add extra hits without a warrior cap, subtract ignored hits, and add one attacker hit if defender has no warriors. Vagabond is defenseless instead when it has no undamaged swords.
rulings.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle

rulings.ruling: Each hit removes one opposing piece; the side taking hits chooses removal order but must remove all its warriors before its buildings/tokens. That side also chooses the order of effects triggered by its own pieces’ removal. Both sides deal their counted hits, and warrior losses do not retroactively change rolled-hit caps. A player removing an enemy building or token scores one VP each, including when defending or outside battle. Vagabond takes hits as item damage instead.
rulings.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle

Q04.question: How do crafting costs, repeat use of crafting pieces, absent supply items and duplicate persistent effects work?

rulings.ruling: Craft a card from hand when allowed by your faction, paying each bottom-left icon with a crafting piece whose clearing suit matches that icon; the card’s suit does not set the cost. Marquise, Eyrie, and Alliance use one workshop, roost, or sympathy respectively per icon, and each piece activates at most once per turn. A three-color question-mark icon accepts any suit.
rulings.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle

rulings.ruling: An item card cannot be crafted if its corresponding item token is absent from the map supply.
rulings.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle

rulings.ruling: Only an identical persistent effect already in your own play area bars crafting that effect again. Another player’s copy does not bar it.
rulings.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle

Q07.question: For standard two-player setup, what deck change, hand size, ruins/item setup and faction setup order apply?

rulings.ruling: In a two-player game, remove all four dominance cards, shuffle the shared deck, and deal each player three cards.

Cover the four R building slots with ruins. Put the separate map item supply (2 boots, 2 bags, 1 crossbow, 1 hammer, 2 swords, 2 tea, 2 coins) in its corresponding map spaces. Only if Vagabond is present, its setup hides one R-marked bag, boot, hammer, and sword, one beneath each ruin: shuffle the four stacks with identities hidden and return each to an empty R slot. Without Vagabond, ruins contain no items.
Set up factions in letter order: Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond. This setup order is distinct from turn order.

Q15.question: How do Alliance Revolt and Spread Sympathy differ in timing/order, eligible clearing, supporter cost, martial law and results?

rulings.ruling: Both Revolt and Spread Sympathy occur during Birdsong. Complete all Revolts before starting any Spread Sympathy; either action may be done any number of times. Every supporter spent for either must match the target clearing, with bird cards wild. After spreading starts, you cannot return to Revolt that Birdsong, so newly spread sympathy cannot fund a same-Birdsong Revolt.

Choose a sympathetic clearing without a base, matching a base still on your board; spend two matching supporters. Remove all enemy pieces there, scoring one normal VP per enemy building or token removed, then place the matching base. Place warriors there equal to the number of sympathetic clearings matching that base’s printed suit, including this revolt clearing, and one warrior in the Officers box. If a prompted placement is short, resolve the effect by placing the maximum possible; no additional base-placement prerequisite is added. Enemy Vagabond damages three items instead of being removed.

Choose an unsympathetic clearing adjacent by path to sympathy; if no sympathy is anywhere, choose any clearing. Spend the matching supporters shown above the next sympathy token. If the chosen clearing has at least three warriors of one other player, add one matching supporter for Martial Law. Place the token and score its uncovered VP space. There can be only one sympathy per clearing; the Keep’s placement ban still applies.

Q16.question: How does Alliance train officers and organize, and what does losing a base do to supporters/officers?

rulings.ruling: During Daylight, spend a hand card matching a clearing with a base to place one warrior from supply in the Officers box. Supporters cannot pay Train. Each officer permits one Evening military operation, and operations do not consume officers.

One Organize operation removes one Alliance warrior from an unsympathetic clearing, places sympathy there, and scores the uncovered VP. It costs no supporters and has no adjacency or Martial Law requirement, but token placement must be legal.
Whenever a base is removed, discard all supporters matching its clearing, including birds, and remove half the officers rounded up. If no bases remain, discard excess supporters down to five.

Q19.question: When does a faction become Hostile to Vagabond, when is Infamy scored, can Aid undo Hostility, and what does Strike target?

rulings.ruling: Removing one warrior of a non-Hostile faction immediately makes it Hostile, except the special allied battle-loss rule. During battle on your own turn, Vagabond scores one extra VP per hostile piece removed, excluding the warrior that first caused Hostility. A hostile building or token normally yields two VP in that battle on Vagabond’s turn: one ordinary removal VP plus one Infamy. A hostile warrior yields one Infamy, except the first warrior that caused Hostility; warriors normally give no removal VP. Infamy depends on whose turn it is, not who attacks, and is not scored on another player’s turn or from Strike.

Aid cannot move a Hostile marker out of Hostile, though Vagabond may still take a crafted item. Strike exhausts a crossbow to remove one enemy warrior in the clearing; only if that enemy has no warriors there may it remove another faction piece instead. Check hostility; Strike is not battle and gives no Infamy.

rulings.part: Allied warriors taken as battle hits
rulings.ruling: When using an ally’s warriors as your own in battle, Vagabond may absorb hits by removing those warriors or damaging items. If it removes more allied warriors than items it damages in that battle, the ally becomes Hostile at battle end; equal numbers do not make it Hostile. This special timing overrides the ordinary immediate hostility timing for allied warriors removed as hits against another enemy.

Q20.question: What are coalition eligibility, timing, VP requirement, partner selection and victory, and what changes if partner is Hostile?

rulings.ruling: Vagabond cannot win through normal dominance. With four or more players, during Vagabond’s own Daylight at 10 or more VP, it may activate dominance to form a coalition with another player not already in a coalition. Choose the lowest-VP eligible player other than Vagabond, with choice among ties. An already-activated dominance player is ineligible because they have no score marker on the VP track; compare eligible players still on the track.

Put Vagabond’s score marker on the partner’s faction board and stop scoring VP. If the partner wins, Vagabond also wins, including when the partner later activates and wins through dominance. Coalition partners are not enemies.
If the chosen partner was Hostile, reset that relationship to Indifferent. Coalition does not grant Allied relationship powers.

Q31.question: How do forest adjacency and Winter river affect Vagabond Slip, and does Fall add any special map rule?

rulings.ruling: For Slip, a forest is adjacent to clearings touching it without crossing a printed path, and to forests separated by one printed path. On Winter, the river also divides forests as paths do.
rulings.evidence: Vagabond; Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle

rulings.ruling: Fall has no special rules.

Q44.question: Can Alliance first Spread Sympathy into a clearing and then Revolt there in that same Birdsong?

rulings.ruling: No. Both actions happen in Birdsong, and all Revolts must be completed before any Spread Sympathy begins. Although each can be taken any number of times, once spreading starts, Alliance cannot return to Revolt during that Birdsong. Newly spread sympathy therefore cannot enable a Revolt that same Birdsong.

Q46.question: Does placing warriors in a sympathetic clearing or moving only Vagabond pawn there cause Outrage, and what if allied warriors accompany Vagabond?

rulings.part: Placing warriors or moving Vagabond pawn
rulings.ruling: Placing warriors in a sympathetic clearing does not trigger Outrage. Moving only the Vagabond pawn there does not trigger warrior-entry Outrage. Removing sympathy still triggers Outrage.

Forcing Allied Woodland Alliance warriors to accompany Vagabond into sympathy causes no Outrage; resolve it as the Alliance moving its own warriors. Warriors of another Allied faction entering sympathy do trigger Outrage for that moving faction, paid from that faction’s own hand under normal Outrage rules.

Q48.question: What happens to Vagabond pawn when a revolt or another enemy remove-all-pieces effect hits its clearing?

rulings.part: Pawn under remove-all effects and Revolt
rulings.ruling: The Vagabond pawn is not a warrior, cannot be removed, and remains in the clearing. An effect that removes all enemy pieces there instead damages three Vagabond items. In a Revolt, the Alliance removes all enemy pieces but damages three Vagabond items instead of removing the pawn.

Q60.question: A Vagabond battles a previously non-Hostile faction on its own turn, removes two warriors followed by one building. How much removal/Infamy VP, and why?

rulings.ruling: Total is 3 VP: first warrior, 0 ordinary VP and 0 Infamy because it is the warrior that first makes the faction Hostile; second warrior, 0 ordinary VP plus 1 Infamy VP because the faction is now Hostile; building, 1 ordinary removal VP plus 1 Infamy VP because it is Hostile. Thus 0 + 1 + 2 = 3 VP.

Q78.question: During Alliance Evening, how many military operations may be taken, and for one Recruit operation how many warriors are placed and where?

rulings.ruling: Take up to the number of officers in military operations, in any order and repetition. Officers remain on the board and are not consumed when an operation is taken.
One Recruit operation places one Alliance warrior in one clearing with a base.

Q79.question: How many Daylight actions may the Vagabond take, must the action types follow a fixed order, and may the same action type be repeated?

rulings.ruling: Vagabond has no fixed Daylight action allowance. It may take action types in any order and repeat them, as ready undamaged items permit.

Q80.question: What item and how many of it must the Vagabond exhaust to take the Daylight Strike action, and can an exhausted or damaged copy pay that cost?

rulings.ruling: Strike requires exhausting one crossbow to remove one enemy warrior in the clearing. Only if that enemy has no warriors there may Vagabond remove another piece of its faction instead.
The crossbow must be face up and undamaged to pay the cost; an exhausted (face-down) or damaged crossbow cannot be used.

Q81.question: The Marquise attacks at the Keep with two warriors. The defender plays an unfoiled matching ambush, removing both attacking warriors. The Marquise can pay Field Hospitals. Are the warriors returned before or after the check that ends battle for having no attackers, and does battle continue if Hospitals is paid?

rulings.part: Hospitals timing and whether battle continues
rulings.ruling: Field Hospitals return the two removed Marquise warriors to the Keep clearing immediately when removed, before checking whether the ambush left no attackers. Since Hospitals are paid and the returned warriors remain in the battle clearing, battle continues; it does not end for having no attacking warriors. Marquise pays one card matching the clearing.
rulings.evidence: Actions → Marquise de Cat; FAQ & Rulings

Q19.question: When does a faction become Hostile to Vagabond, when is Infamy scored, can Aid undo Hostility, and what does Strike target?

rulings.ruling: Removing one warrior of a faction that is not already Hostile immediately moves its relationship marker to Hostile, subject to the stated exception for the allied battle-loss rule.

During battle on the Vagabond's own turn, score one extra VP per hostile piece removed, except the warrior that first made that faction Hostile. A hostile building or token removed in battle on the Vagabond's turn normally yields two VP total: one ordinary removal VP and one Infamy. A hostile warrior yields one Infamy except the first warrior that caused Hostility. Infamy applies based on whose turn it is, not which side attacks; none is scored on another player's turn or from Strike.

Aid cannot move a marker out of Hostile, though the Vagabond may still obtain a crafted item. Q20.question: What are coalition eligibility, timing, VP requirement, partner selection and victory, and what changes if partner is Hostile?

rulings.ruling: Vagabond cannot activate a normal dominance win. With four or more players, during its own Daylight at 10 or more VP, it may activate dominance to form a coalition with another eligible player.

Choose a player not already in a coalition who has the lowest VP among players other than the Vagabond; choose among ties. A player who already activated dominance cannot be selected because they have no score marker on the track. Compare eligible players still on the score track.

Q48.question: What happens to Vagabond pawn when a revolt or another enemy remove-all-pieces effect hits its clearing?

rulings.part: Vagabond pawn when all enemy pieces are removed
rulings.ruling: The Vagabond pawn is not removed by an effect that removes all enemy pieces from its clearing; instead, the effect damages three items.

During Alliance Revolt, the enemy Vagabond damages three items instead of being removed. The same three-item damage replacement applies generally when an enemy effect removes all enemy pieces from the pawn's clearing.
rulings.evidence: Woodland Alliance — Revolt; Vagabond — Pawn and items

Q60.question: A Vagabond battles a previously non-Hostile faction on its own turn, removes two warriors followed by one building. How much removal/Infamy VP, and why?

rulings.ruling: The two warriors yield 0 ordinary removal VP. Removing the first warrior makes the previously non-Hostile faction Hostile, but that first warrior is excluded from Infamy; the second hostile warrior removed in the Vagabond's own-turn battle adds 1 Infamy VP. Warrior contribution: 0 ordinary VP + 1 Infamy VP = 1 VP.
rulings.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions — Ordinary removal VP; Vagabond — Hostile and Infamy

rulings.ruling: The building is removed after the faction is Hostile, so it gives 1 ordinary removal VP plus 1 Infamy VP = 2 VP. Total: warriors 0 ordinary + 1 Infamy; building 1 ordinary + 1 Infamy; 3 VP. The first warrior that caused Hostility is not eligible for Infamy.
rulings.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions — Ordinary removal VP; Vagabond — Hostile and Infamy

Q78.question: During Alliance Evening, how many military operations may be taken, and for one Recruit operation how many warriors are placed and where?

rulings.ruling: Take up to the number of officers you have in military operations, in any order and with repetition allowed. Officers remain on the board and are not consumed by taking operations.
One Recruit operation places one warrior in one clearing with an Alliance base.

Q79.question: How many Daylight actions may the Vagabond take, must the action types follow a fixed order, and may the same action type be repeated?

rulings.part: Number and order of Vagabond Daylight actions
rulings.ruling: The Vagabond may take Daylight actions in any order and any number, as ready undamaged items permit. There is no fixed sequence by action type, and an action type may be repeated if its item costs and other requirements can be paid.

Q80.question: What item and how many of it must the Vagabond exhaust to take the Daylight Strike action, and can an exhausted or damaged copy pay that cost?

rulings.ruling: Strike requires exhausting one crossbow and removes one enemy warrior in the clearing. Only if that enemy has no warriors in the clearing may Strike remove another piece of that faction instead. Check hostility; Strike is not battle and gives no Infamy.
The crossbow used to pay must be face up and undamaged so it can be exhausted. An exhausted or damaged crossbow cannot pay the cost.

Are the warriors returned before or after the check that ends battle for having no attackers, and does battle continue if Hospitals is paid?

rulings.part: Timing of Hospitals versus ending check
rulings.ruling: The Marquise may spend a card matching the clearing immediately when the two warriors are removed by the unfoiled ambush. Field Hospitals return them to the Keep clearing before checking whether the ambush left no attacking warriors or pawns.

rulings.ruling: Yes. In the given scenario both attacking warriors are returned to the Keep clearing, so attacking warriors remain and battle continues instead of ending for lack of attackers.
